sender: Tom Verhaege, Software Sales Trading, Brackley Hume Securities
subject: Sales color: Stratavue (STVU) FQ2 - share of new workloads landing on Azure moved up, capacity waits mentioned (MSFT read?)
body:
Ellen, Raj, Marcus,

Quick color from yesterday's Stratavue Data (STVU) FQ2 print and call. Not our analyst's main focus, but a couple of comments looked worth passing along ahead of MSFT on the 28th.

What Stratavue said (the company is a data platform vendor that runs on all three major clouds):
- Share of new customer consumption landing on Azure was 38% in FQ2 vs. 31% a year ago and 34% last quarter. AWS ~44%, Google Cloud ~18%.
- The CFO said two large enterprise customers 'waited several weeks for GPU-adjacent capacity in two U.S. regions' before going live on Azure. She described this as 'a capacity story, not a demand one.'
- Management attributed the share shift mostly to customers already committed to Azure through enterprise agreements who prefer to burn down commitments on partner data platforms.
- FQ3 consumption guide was raised 3 points at the midpoint.

Caveats:
- This is one vendor's customer mix, not Azure revenue. The base is small, and a handful of large accounts can move a 4-point swing.
- The commit-burn-down point could also mean pull-forward of existing spend rather than new workload growth.
- Stratavue did not give any dollar figures on Azure-sourced consumption.

Why it may matter: If other data and app vendors report similar Azure share gains in the next two weeks, that would support the Azure consumption picture ahead of the print. Worth keeping on the radar, and we'd want a second vendor before drawing conclusions. Happy to pull transcripts for Hexalane and two other multi-cloud names that report next week.
